body.x: Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley technology outlet, named Doosan Robotics, DOGU Robotics and Rezbin Waste Technology, Inc. its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech Into Reality," the third edition combined the Daegu International Future Auto & Mobility Expo (DIFA), the Daegu Robot Expo (ROBEX), the ICT Convergence Expo Korea (ITCE) and start-up programs. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

body.cap: Eliane Fiolet, Ubergizmo's co-founder and editor-in-chief, joined the global media press corps for FIX 2026. Ubergizmo also visited Daegu for FIX 2025.

body.x: Ubergizmo launched in Silicon Valley in 2005 as a global technology outlet. It covers IT products such as smartphones and consumer electronics, along with AI, the internet of things (IoT), augmented and virtual reality (AR and VR), drones and automotive technology. It reports from major technology shows and evaluates design, user experience, practicality and market competitiveness as well as performance.

body.cap: The FIX 2026 Global Media Awards ceremony at the Future Innovation tech eXpo | Photo - AVING News

body.x: In a pre-show interview for FIX 2026, Ubergizmo said technology is moving beyond laboratory demonstrations into systems that run reliably in factories, on roads and in daily life. It called Physical AI, where industrial AI, autonomous mobility and robotics converge, a key technology trend, and said it expects humanoid and service robots, advanced sensing and mobility innovation to be applied in real industry and daily life.

Ubergizmo's three selections cover industrial automation with collaborative robots, facility security with AI-powered patrol robots, and plastic waste management with a rewards-based recycling platform.

body.x: Doosan Robotics Supplies Collaborative Robots for Manufacturing, Logistics and Services

Doosan Robotics develops and supplies collaborative robots designed to share workspaces with people. Its robot solutions automate repetitive and precision work in manufacturing, and also in logistics, services and other industries.

Collaborative robots work alongside operators in the same space, which makes it easier to build flexible work environments and switch processes than with conventional industrial robots. As manufacturers diversify their product lines and demand for high-mix, low-volume production grows, integrating robots efficiently into existing workflows matters more.

body.cap: The FIX 2026 Global Media Awards ceremony at the Future Innovation tech eXpo | Photo - AVING News

body.x: Doosan Robotics offers a lineup for different payloads and work environments and tailors robot solutions to each customer's process. On its official website, the company lists precision control using its six proprietary torque sensors and Dart-Suite, a software platform for robot operation, as core capabilities. It sells and services robots through a global network and said it operates in 45 countries across the United States, Europe and Asia.

Doosan Robotics planned to show Scan&Go at ROBEX 2026, the 15th Daegu Robot Expo. Scan&Go combines a collaborative robot arm and an autonomous mobile robot (AMR) with Physical AI and 3D vision. It scans the surfaces of large composite structures such as turbine blades, aircraft fuselages and building exteriors, and generates work paths from on-site information for inspection, sanding and grinding. According to the company, Scan&Go won a Best of Innovation award in the artificial intelligence category and was named an honoree in the robotics category at the CES 2026 Innovation Awards.
Collaborative robots now handle assembly, inspection, handling and packaging, not just simple repetitive tasks.

body.x: DOGU Robotics Patrols Facilities With AI Autonomous Security Robots

DOGU Robotics provides AI-based autonomous security robots under its ASR (AI-powered Security Robot) service, along with integrated security operations solutions. CEO Jinhyo Kim, who studied autonomous robots in graduate school, founded the company in 2017, and it is headquartered in Daegu. It set up a U.S. subsidiary, DOGU, Inc., in 2024 to enter the North American market from Silicon Valley, and it has a Southeast Asia base in Singapore hosted at Infineon Technologies.

Its robots patrol the inside and outside of facilities, combining remote monitoring, risk detection and data analysis to support safety management at industrial facilities, logistics centers, hospitals and public buildings. Facility security has long relied on CCTV, fixed sensors and patrols by staff. Fixed equipment is limited by where it is installed and what it can see, and patrolling a large facility around the clock takes staff and operating costs. Autonomous security robots offer an alternative that combines mobile surveillance with remote monitoring.

body.cap: The FIX 2026 Global Media Awards ceremony at the Future Innovation tech eXpo | Photo - AVING News

body.x: DOGU develops both the patrol robots and the software that runs them. Its lineup includes iroi, an indoor patrol robot with a 21-inch touch display and an ultraviolet sterilization lamp; Patrover, an outdoor patrol robot; and Robjet, a modular robot built from function modules. SOS (Security Operation System), its integrated monitoring system, lets operators manage multiple robots from one place and respond to anomalies the robots detect. Its 3D navigation technology lets robots patrol multi-story buildings. DOGU also developed a quadruped patrol robot solution with Rainbow Robotics for stairs and rough terrain.

According to the company, DOGU has supplied robots to the Korean National Police Agency, POSCO, LG Electronics, KT, S-1 and SK shieldus, and it operates at more than 100 sites nationwide. The United States is its main export market: iroi is deployed at SK hynix America, and DOGU has a long-term service contract with Dolby for its Sunnyvale site. In July 2026, it signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Robot.com and exported about USD 2 million worth of robots, including iroi. DOGU, which also showed iroi at FIX 2024, took part in ROBEX 2026 and planned to demonstrate humanoids from Robot.com, including R-noid, alongside its quadruped patrol solution.
Rezbin Rewards Plastic Recycling Through a Mobile App

Rezbin Waste Technology, Inc., a Philippine recycling technology company that co-exhibited at the ASEAN-KOREA STARTUP WEEK 2026 booth at FIX 2026, runs a rewards-based system that encourages plastic recycling and supports waste management. It tracks participation, such as sorting or donating plastic at offices, schools and residential facilities, so users earn points for recycling and exchange them for rewards.

Tackling plastic waste takes more than recycling technology and collection and processing infrastructure. It also requires sustained participation from citizens and companies from the disposal stage. People may know recycling helps the environment yet find it hard to keep doing it when their efforts go unrecognized.

Rezbin built a mobile app that tracks recycling participation and rewards it. Users manage points earned by donating or recycling plastic and can exchange them for partner rewards. The company offers a solution for building waste management programs at offices, schools and residential facilities, and says its goal is to make recycling an everyday habit.
Three Selections Across Industry, Security and Recycling

Doosan Robotics automates tasks in manufacturing, logistics and services with collaborative robots. DOGU Robotics combines autonomous driving, risk detection and remote monitoring in its security robots. Rezbin encourages plastic recycling through a mobile tracking and rewards system.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including Ubergizmo. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a first-generation Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, CEO of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run multinational general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, China's first outlet for IT, enterprise digital transformation and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, editor-in-chief of Pokde.net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners take part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and plan to report to international audiences on innovative Korean companies in future industries.
